vsaq.question: Define Physics.
vsaq.answer: Physics studies matter, energy and their interactions through observation, experiment and mathematical laws.

vsaq.question: Write the key relation or statement for Absolute error.
vsaq.answer: For repeated readings, absolute error is the magnitude of the difference between a reading and the mean value.

vsaq.question: Define Relative error.
vsaq.answer: Relative error equals mean absolute error divided by the mean measured value; percentage error is 100 times this ratio.

laq.question: Explain the types of measurement errors and the rules for combining them.
laq.answer:
Principle: Begin with the relevant physical law and state the assumptions.

Errors may be systematic, random or due to instrument least count. For readings a₁…aₙ, mean ā = Σaᵢ/n and mean absolute error Δa = Σ|aᵢ−ā|/n. Report a = ā ± Δa.

For z = x ± y, absolute errors add: Δz = Δx + Δy. For z = xy or x/y, fractional errors add: Δz/z = Δx/x + Δy/y. For z = xⁿ, Δz/z = |n|Δx/x. State units and round uncertainty to sensible significant figures.

laq.question: Describe dimensional analysis and discuss its uses and limitations.
laq.answer:
Principle: Begin with the relevant physical law and state the assumptions.

Write each quantity as MᵃLᵇTᶜ. Equate exponents on both sides using dimensional homogeneity. This checks dimensional consistency, converts units and can obtain the form of a relation up to a dimensionless constant.

It cannot determine numerical constants, distinguish quantities with identical dimensions, decide additive terms or prove an equation physically correct. Trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic arguments must be dimensionless.

laq.question: Explain significant figures and the rules used in calculations.
laq.answer:
Principle: Begin with the relevant physical law and state the assumptions.

All non-zero digits are significant; zeros between non-zero digits are significant; leading zeros are not; trailing zeros after a decimal are significant. In multiplication/division retain the least number of significant figures. In addition/subtraction retain the least number of decimal places.

Round only at the end: discard below 5, increase the last retained digit for above 5, and follow the prescribed rounding convention for an exact 5.

laq.question: Derive the three equations of uniformly accelerated motion.
laq.answer:
Principle: Begin with the relevant physical law and state the assumptions.

From a = (v−u)/t, obtain v = u + at. Average velocity for uniform acceleration is (u+v)/2, hence s = (u+v)t/2. Substituting v = u+at gives s = ut + ½at².

Eliminate t using t=(v−u)/a in s=(u+v)t/2 to obtain v² = u² + 2as. Mention that these equations apply only to constant acceleration along a straight line.

Scoring finish: Define every symbol, check dimensions, include SI units and box the final expression.

laq.question: Explain position–time and velocity–time graphs and obtain displacement from them.
laq.answer:
Principle: Begin with the relevant physical law and state the assumptions.

The slope of an x–t graph gives velocity; a horizontal line means rest and a straight inclined line means constant velocity. The slope of a v–t graph gives acceleration.

The signed area under the v–t curve between two instants equals displacement because ∫v dt = Δx. Area under a speed–time graph gives distance. For constant acceleration, the rectangular and triangular areas give s = ut + ½at².

Scoring finish: Define every symbol, check dimensions, include SI units and box the final expression.

laq.question: Discuss free fall as uniformly accelerated motion.
laq.answer:
Principle: Begin with the relevant physical law and state the assumptions.

Choose upward as positive. Near Earth, acceleration is a = −g. Therefore v = u−gt, y = ut−½gt² and v² = u²−2gy. For a body dropped from rest, u=0 and downward distance h=½gt².

At the highest point of upward projection v=0, so time of ascent u/g and maximum height u²/(2g). Neglect air resistance.

Scoring finish: Define every symbol, check dimensions, include SI units and box the final expression.

laq.question: Derive the trajectory, time of flight, maximum height and range of a projectile.
laq.answer:
Principle: Begin with the relevant physical law and state the assumptions.

Resolve u into u cosθ horizontally and u sinθ vertically. Then x=u cosθ·t and y=u sinθ·t−½gt². Eliminating t gives y=x tanθ−gx²/(2u²cos²θ), a parabola.

Putting y=0 gives T=2u sinθ/g. At the top vᵧ=0, hence H=u²sin²θ/(2g). Range R=(u cosθ)T=u²sin2θ/g. Maximum range u²/g occurs at 45°.

Scoring finish: Define every symbol, check dimensions, include SI units and box the final expression.
laq.keyPoints: Derive • the • trajectory, • time • of • flight, • maximum • height

laq.question: Explain addition and resolution of vectors by analytical method.
laq.answer:
Principle: Begin with the relevant physical law and state the assumptions.

Let A=Aₓi+Aᵧj and B=Bₓi+Bᵧj. Their resultant R=(Aₓ+Bₓ)i+(Aᵧ+Bᵧ)j. Hence R=√(Rₓ²+Rᵧ²) and tanφ=Rᵧ/Rₓ, with the quadrant checked.

A vector A making angle θ with x-axis resolves as A cosθ along x and A sinθ along y. Components are independent and add algebraically.

Scoring finish: Define every symbol, check dimensions, include SI units and box the final expression.

laq.question: Derive centripetal acceleration in uniform circular motion.
laq.answer:
Principle: Begin with the relevant physical law and state the assumptions.

Two velocity vectors separated by a small angle Δθ have change Δv ≈ vΔθ directed toward the centre. Since Δθ=Δs/r=vΔt/r, acceleration a=lim(Δv/Δt)=v²/r.

Using v=rω gives a=ω²r. The velocity is tangential while acceleration and net force are radially inward.

Scoring finish: Define every symbol, check dimensions, include SI units and box the final expression.

laq.answer:
Principle: Begin with the relevant physical law and state the assumptions.

First law defines inertial frames. Second law states F=dp/dt. For constant mass, p=mv, so F=m(dv/dt)=ma. Third law states F_AB=−F_BA; the pair acts on different bodies.

Always isolate one body, draw all external forces, choose axes and apply ΣFₓ=maₓ and ΣFᵧ=maᵧ. Action–reaction forces must never be placed on the same free-body diagram.

laq.question: Explain friction on a rough inclined plane and obtain the angle of repose.
laq.answer:
Principle: Begin with the relevant physical law and state the assumptions.

For a body on an incline θ, resolve weight into mg sinθ down the plane and mg cosθ normal to it. Thus N=mg cosθ. At impending downward motion, limiting friction μₛN acts upward.

Equilibrium gives mg sinθ=μₛmg cosθ, so tanθ=μₛ. This limiting θ is the angle of repose. Friction is self-adjusting below this limit.

laq.question: Derive conservation of linear momentum for two interacting bodies.
laq.answer:
Principle: Begin with the relevant physical law and state the assumptions.

For bodies 1 and 2, Newton’s third law gives F₁₂=−F₂₁. By the second law, dp₁/dt=−dp₂/dt, hence d(p₁+p₂)/dt=0. Therefore p₁+p₂ is constant.

For a collision, m₁u₁+m₂u₂=m₁v₁+m₂v₂ provided external impulse is negligible.

1. Sensor: A sensor converts a physical quantity such as light, pressure or temperature into a usable signal.
2. Internet of Things: IoT connects sensor-equipped devices so they can collect, exchange and act on data.

laq.answer:

Sensors measure the environment and convert physical inputs into electrical or digital signals. A controller processes these signals using programmed logic or a trained model. Actuators then convert control commands into motion or another physical output.

Feedback repeats this loop, allowing correction of error. Give examples such as a line-following robot or an automated medical device, and mention safety interlocks.

laq.question: Explain quantum tunnelling and give technological applications.
laq.answer:
Principle: Begin with the relevant physical law and state the assumptions.

A quantum particle is described by a wavefunction that can penetrate a finite potential barrier. Its amplitude decays inside the barrier but may remain non-zero beyond it, giving a finite transmission probability even when classical energy is lower than barrier height.

Applications include tunnel diodes, scanning tunnelling microscopy, flash-memory operation and nuclear alpha decay. Tunnelling probability falls rapidly with barrier width and height.

laq.question: Discuss artificial intelligence and machine learning with benefits, limits and responsible use.
laq.answer:
Principle: Begin with the relevant physical law and state the assumptions.

Machine learning trains a model on examples to detect patterns and make predictions; AI is the broader field that uses such models with perception, reasoning and action. Applications include medical-image assistance, weather prediction, adaptive learning and industrial quality control.

Models can inherit bias, make confident errors and threaten privacy. Responsible use requires quality data, testing, transparency, security, human oversight and energy-aware design.
